sampling_model.design: Observational i.i.d. sampling from an unknown law in \(\mathcal M_{d,K}\).
sampling_model.treatment: \(A_i\in[K]\) is logged with unknown \(e_{ax}\) satisfying only \(e_{ax}\ge1/(2K)\) on positive-mass groups; the simplex constraint permits propensities larger than \(2/K\).
sampling_model.overlap: Menu-scaled lower overlap is imposed only on \(x\) with \(p_x>0\); null groups and unobserved sample cells are legal.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The upper bound must estimate or avoid both unknown \(p_x\) and unknown \(e_{ax}\); known-uniform subexperiments may be used only for the converse.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: HAVER uses a lower-confidence pivot and head averaging to obtain instance-dependent MSE upper bounds for passive maximum-mean estimation.
Theorem 7 proves that a \(1/14\)-uniform approximation to Boolean OR has degree at least \(\sqrt K\).
The paper characterizes pathwise differentiability of optimal value and gives online one-step inference under fixed-complexity asymptotics.

The static optimal-value theorem proves asymptotic linearity, and asymptotic normality when the influence variance is positive, for an independent-sample de-biased softmax estimator under \(\delta\)-polynomial suboptimality-gap density, \(\beta_n=\omega(n^{1/[2(1+\delta)]})\), stated \(L^2\) nuisance convergence and product-rate conditions, and uniform boundedness.
The paper combines smooth--nonsmooth splitting, polynomial approximation, factorial moments, and fuzzy hypotheses for additive discrete-distribution functionals.
The paper uses best-polynomial and moment-matching duality to derive the all-regime entropy MSE and its consistency threshold.
The paper proves multi-action policy-regret bounds over restricted policy classes using doubly robust scores.

tldr: A growing treatment menu turns each sparse patient group into a high-dimensional nonsmooth maximum with random denominators. The headline kernel is the explicit all-regime minimax MSE \(r_\star(n,d,K)\), with a total statistically computable estimator on the full unknown-mass class under menu-scaled lower overlap alone and a matching same-class converse. The mathematical hinge is a dimension-uniform certificate that makes maximum-approximation bias, exact factorial-lift covariance, and normalized moment-prior mixture geometry share one evaluated scale, while exposing the finite coefficient count \(M_{2K,L}=\binom{2K+L}{L}\) and the estimator's combinatorial evaluation cost. Supporting claims cover the one-group and \(K\ge d^2\) rates and a new binary-to-many-arm hardness transfer; the accepted \(K=2\) frontier is used only as a cited boundary condition. The open content is the exact transition for \(2<K<d^2\) and the resulting necessary-and-sufficient consistency boundary.

project_justification.gap: The literature separates fixed-dimensional nonregular inference, restricted-class policy regret, one-group maximum-mean upper bounds, and scalar approximation-theoretic minimax estimation; none gives the joint finite-sample risk when sparse categorical groups and treatments grow together under unknown observational logging and only a menu-scaled lower propensity bound.
project_justification.niche: The categorical experiment has exact Poisson factorial and likelihood-mixture identities, but its \(K\)-way tie fan, arbitrary group occupancy, and potentially unbalanced logging require a dimension-uniform primal--dual certificate with an explicit finite representation.
project_justification.fill: The project evaluates that certificate, splices it to the supporting one-group and many-arm results, the new binary-grouping transfer, and the cited \(K=2\) boundary, then turns the closed-form envelope into a total computable estimator, an all-estimator lower bound, and exact consistency and parametric-MSE conditions.

related_work: LuedtkeVanderLaan2016 supplies the standard identification and nonregularity boundary: its pathwise-differentiability theorem and online estimator explain why exact ties defeat ordinary first-order inference, but identification is not an originality target here and the paper does not address growing-dimensional minimax MSE. WhitehouseAusternSyrgkanis2025 is an informed-by comparison rather than a theorem target. Its static theorem assumes independent evaluation data; a \(\delta\)-polynomial density for every suboptimality gap, allowing an atom at zero; \(\beta_n=\omega(n^{1/[2(1+\delta)]})\); \(\lVert\widehat Q_n-Q^\star\rVert_2=o_P(n^{-1/4}\beta_n^{-1/2})\); a product nuisance error of \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\); \(L^2\) consistency; uniform boundedness; and positive influence variance for the normal limit. The unrestricted finite-sample class here assumes none of the density or nuisance-rate conditions and permits both dimensions to grow. NguyenBarrettJun2025HAVER is the closest estimator comparator: its lower-confidence pivot and head averaging control passive one-group MSE, but random patient-group counts, unknown masses, causal logging, and a global converse are absent. JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 supplies the nonsmooth--smooth split, factorial-moment lift, clipping, and fuzzy-hypothesis architecture. WuYang2016 supplies the stronger requirement that approximation and moment-matched priors be governed by the same extremal quantity, including an evaluated consistency threshold. CaiLow2011 supplies the moment-prior and chi-square template for a kinked functional. Spalek2008 is the obstruction comparator: its explicit dual polynomial shows that a uniform maximum surrogate cannot hide \(K\) in its degree. LuedtkeVanderLaan2018 studies maxima with a possibly growing index set under asymptotic remainder conditions, not sparse-table all-regime risk. ZhouAtheyWager2023 concerns learned-policy regret over restricted classes and motivates lower overlap, but it is a consumer-facing neighbor rather than a theorem-level target.
technical_internal_limitation: The early Boolean check for \(K=64\) gives numerical best errors approximately \(0.784421\), \(0.500867\), and \(0.412390\) at degrees \(4\), \(7\), and \(8\), respectively. These floating-point linear programs are reconnaissance only. The rigorous content is the OR obstruction in \(\mathrm{lem{:}or\text{-}obstruction}\) and the exact lifted-variance identity in \(\mathrm{lem{:}poisson\text{-}lift\text{-}identity}\). A degree-\(L\) local lift has \(M_{2K,L}=\binom{2K+L}{L}\) coefficients in the full observed-cell representation, so the displayed evaluation routine is finite but may be exponential in \(K\) or \(L\). No polynomial-time theorem is claimed, and a proposed solution that suppresses this dependence fails the kernel.
honest_scope: The full joint rate \(r_\star(n,d,K)\), the attaining estimator \(\widehat V_\star\), and the exact consistency boundary are open objects isolated in \(\mathrm{oeq{:}joint\text{-}frontier}\). The proof obligations retained in the core are the lower-overlap full-class empirical upper bound, the centered-winner lower envelope, the matched region \(K\ge d^2\), the one-group benchmark, and the binary-to-many-arm transfer. The accepted \(K=2\) frontier and standard causal identification are cited boundary conditions, not originality or solve targets. Total statistical computability is required through a finite coefficient table, exact certificate generation, and the displayed dense evaluation bound; polynomial-time computation is not claimed. The paper does not claim inference for a learned policy, a budget curve, sharp leading constants, or honest confidence intervals. The \(d=2,K=3\) witness verifies that unequal logging and switching maximizing arms remain inside the enlarged lower-overlap-only class.

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent and identically distributed with common observed-data margin induced by \(P\).

standard.name: Generic lower-overlap motivation (the menu-scaled normalization is specific to this note)

definitions.name: Causal law class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_{d,K}=\{P: Y=Y(A)\ P\text{-a.s.},\ (Y(1),\ldots,Y(K))\perp A\mid X,\ e_{ax}\ge1/(2K)\text{ for all }x\text{ with }p_x>0\text{ and all }a\in[K]\}\), for every \(d\ge1\) and \(K\ge2\).

definitions.name: Joint minimax MSE
definitions.construction: \(R(n,d,K)=\inf_{\widehat V}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,K}}E_{P^n}[(\widehat V-V^\star(P))^2]\), where the infimum ranges over all measurable estimators based on \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\).

definitions.name: Total empirical cell-weighted maximum
definitions.construction: \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{ER}}=\sum_{x=1}^d(N_x/n)\max_{a\in[K]}\overline Y_{xa}\), with the declared zero convention for every empty arm and hence for every unobserved group.

definitions.name: Balanced-Poisson unbiased polynomial lift
definitions.construction: Write the finite monomial representation as \(P_L(\theta)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_{K,L}}c_\alpha\theta^\alpha\) and set \(U_{P_L}=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_{K,L}}c_\alpha\prod_{a=1}^K H_{\alpha_a}(N_{a0},N_{a1};\lambda)\). Compute \(H_0,\ldots,H_L\) for each arm by the finite convolution \([z^h](1+2z)^{N_{a1}}(1-2z)^{N_{a0}}=\sum_{r=0}^h\binom{N_{a1}}r\binom{N_{a0}}{h-r}2^r(-2)^{h-r}\). Given the coefficient table, dense exact evaluation uses at most \(C_0\{K L^2+L M_{K,L}\}\) arithmetic operations and \(C_0\{K L+M_{K,L}\}\) stored scalars for an absolute implementation constant \(C_0\).

definitions.name: Finite observed-cell factorial lift
definitions.construction: For independent \(N_j\sim\operatorname{Pois}(m q_j)\), define \(G_h(N_j;z_j,m)=\sum_{r=0}^h\binom hr(-z_j)^{h-r}(N_j)_r/m^r\). If \(Q_L(q-z)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_{2K,L}}\gamma_\alpha(q-z)^\alpha\), set \(U_{Q_L}=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal A_{2K,L}}\gamma_\alpha\prod_{j=1}^{2K}G_{\alpha_j}(N_j;z_j,m)\). Given the coefficient table, recursively computing the falling factorials and evaluating the dense sum uses at most \(C_2\{K L^2+L M_{2K,L}\}\) arithmetic operations and \(C_2\{K L+M_{2K,L}\}\) stored scalars.

definitions.name: Dimension-uniform joint certificate handle
definitions.construction:
Construct \(\mathfrak J(d,K,\lambda,L)\) by evaluating a localized polynomial \(Q_L\) for the full lower-overlap ratio maximum \(F_K(q)\) together with the exact second-moment cost of \(U_{Q_L}\). On the balanced comparison slice, reduce this object to the primal pair \(\mathcal E_K(P_L)^2+d^{-1}\mathcal W_{K,\lambda}(P_L)\) over \((c_\alpha:\alpha\in\mathcal A_{K,L})\), and match it to the dual pair \(\Delta_{\max}(
u_0,
u_1)^2\) and \(\mathfrak D_{K,\lambda}(
u_0,
u_1)\) over normalized moment-matched priors. Use exact semialgebraic decision on compact rational localization boxes to certify the primal continuous-domain inequalities, localize \(\lambda\) to empirical patient-group occupancy, and splice the cited \(K=2\), one-group, and saturation boundaries.

definitions.name: Derived sharp frontier scale
definitions.construction: \(r_\star(n,d,K)\) is the explicit dimension-uniform, piecewise-closed rate representative derived by \(\mathrm{oeq{:}joint\text{-}frontier}\), including its logarithmic, transition, and saturation branches.

definitions.name: Attaining-estimator handle
definitions.construction: Construct \(\widehat V_\star\) by sample splitting for localization, a smooth-region bias correction, and on each nonsmooth patient group the finite observed-cell lift \(U_{Q_L}\) with coefficient table indexed by \(\mathcal A_{2K,L}\) and certified by \(\mathfrak J(d,K,\lambda,L)\); combine the group contributions with empirical weights and clip to \([0,1]\). Once the tables are generated, dense evaluation on the sample uses at most \(C_1[n+d\{K L^2+L M_{2K,L}\}]\) arithmetic operations and \(C_1d\{K L+M_{2K,L}\}\) stored scalars. Exact semialgebraic generation of the finite primal coefficient tables and this evaluation give total statistical computability; because \(M_{2K,L}=\binom{2K+L}{L}\), no polynomial-time claim in \((n,d,K)\) is made.

definitions.name: Binary-to-many-arm grouping channel
definitions.construction: Partition \([K]\) into fixed blocks \(G_0,G_1\) of sizes \(g_0=\lfloor K/2\rfloor\) and \(g_1=\lceil K/2\rceil\). Given a binary observation \((X,B,Y)\), \(\mathsf G_K\) draws \(A\) uniformly from \(G_B\), independently of \(Y\) conditional on \((X,B)\), and outputs \((X,A,Y)\); every arm in \(G_b\) inherits the conditional outcome mean of binary treatment \(b\), and a full-data completion draws arm potential outcomes with those inherited means independently of \(A\) conditional on \(X\).

definitions.name: Unequal-logging switching-winner witness
definitions.construction: For \(d=2\) and \(K=3\), let \(p_1=p_2=1/2\), \((e_{11},e_{21},e_{31})=(1/2,1/3,1/6)\), \((e_{12},e_{22},e_{32})=(1/6,1/3,1/2)\), \((\mu_{11},\mu_{21},\mu_{31})=(9/10,1/2,1/5)\), and \((\mu_{12},\mu_{22},\mu_{32})=(1/4,3/5,41/50)\); conditionally on \(X\), draw the Bernoulli potential outcomes independently with these means, draw \(A\) independently from the displayed propensity vector, and set \(Y=Y(A)\).

statements.statement: In the balanced Poisson comparison experiment, \(E_\theta[U_{P_L}]=P_L(\theta)\) and \(\operatorname{Var}_\theta(U_{P_L})=\sum_{\alpha\ne0}(4\lambda)^{-|\alpha|}(D^\alpha P_L(\theta))^2/\alpha!\) for every \(P_L\) and every \(\theta\in[-1/4,1/4]^K\).
statements.justification: The derivative-weighted identity exposes every treatment-menu covariance term, while the finite coefficient representation makes the corresponding statistic executable.
statements.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 uses factorial moments coordinatewise; this identity is the multivariate covariance accounting needed for the \(K\)-ary maximum.
statements.consumer: The open joint certificate can reject approximants with acceptable uniform error but explosive lifted variance.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix an arm \(a\).  Introduce the exponential generating function
\[
 \mathcal H_a(u):=\sum_{h\geq 0}H_h\frac{u^h}{h!}
 =\left(1+\frac{u}{2\lambda}\right)^{N_{a1}}
  \left(1-\frac{u}{2\lambda}\right)^{N_{a0}}.
\]
The equality is coefficientwise exactly the construction in \(\mathrm{def{:}polynomial\text{-}lift}\).  The two Poisson means in the balanced experiment are \(\lambda(1/2+\theta_a)\) and \(\lambda(1/2-\theta_a)\).  Hence the Poisson probability generating function gives, in a neighborhood of zero,
\[
 E_\theta[\mathcal H_a(u)]
 =\exp\!\left\{\lambda(1/2+\theta_a)\frac{u}{2\lambda}
                 -\lambda(1/2-\theta_a)\frac{u}{2\lambda}\right\}
 =e^{\theta_a u}.
\]
Coefficient comparison yields \(E_\theta[H_h]=\theta_a^h\).  The same calculation with two indeterminates gives
\[
 E_\theta[\mathcal H_a(u)\mathcal H_a(v)]
 =\exp\!\left\{\theta_a(u+v)+\frac{uv}{4\lambda}\right\}.
\]
All coefficient extractions and expectations may be interchanged because only finitely many coefficients are needed and Poisson variables have moments of every order.  Therefore
\[
 E_\theta[H_hH_t]
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\{h,t\}}
   \binom h\ell\binom t\ell\ell!(4\lambda)^{-\ell}
   \theta_a^{h+t-2\ell}.
\]

For a multi-index \(\gamma\), write \(H_\gamma=\prod_{a=1}^K H_{\gamma_a}\).  Independence across arms and the preceding identity imply
\[
 E_\theta[H_\gamma H_\delta]
 =\sum_{\alpha\leq\gamma\wedge\delta}
 (4\lambda)^{-|\alpha|}\alpha!
 \binom\gamma\alpha\binom\delta\alpha
 \theta^{\gamma+\delta-2\alpha}.
\]
Using the finite representation \(P_L(\theta)=\sum_\gamma c_\gamma\theta^\gamma\), the first-moment identity gives
\[
 E_\theta[U_{P_L}]=\sum_\gamma c_\gamma\theta^\gamma=P_L(\theta).
\]
Moreover,
\[
 D^\alpha P_L(\theta)
 =\sum_{\gamma\geq\alpha}c_\gamma\,\alpha!\binom\gamma\alpha
   \theta^{\gamma-\alpha}.
\]
Substitution into the preceding second-moment formula and regrouping the finite sums gives
\[
 E_\theta[U_{P_L}^2]
 =\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^K}
   \frac{(4\lambda)^{-|\alpha|}}{\alpha!}
   \{D^\alpha P_L(\theta)\}^2.
\]
The term \(\alpha=0\) is \(P_L(\theta)^2\).  Subtracting the squared expectation proves the stated variance identity.  Derivatives of order above \(L\) vanish, so the displayed sum is finite.  The coefficient table has \(M_{K,L}\) entries and the lift is the finite executable map specified in \(\mathrm{def{:}polynomial\text{-}lift}\).

statements.justification: The identity makes mixture indistinguishability use the same weighted multi-index geometry as the estimator variance.
statements.gap: WuYang2016 and CaiLow2011 use scalar moment matching; neither source supplies this \(K\)-variate exponential kernel with normalized priors for the ratio-max experiment.
statements.consumer: A matching converse can be certified without hiding treatment-menu dependence in a generic total-variation bound.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(\theta\in[-1/4,1/4]^K\), all Poisson means are positive.  Relative to \(P_0\), cancellation of the Poisson exponential factors gives the likelihood ratio
\[
 \Lambda_\theta:=\frac{dP_\theta}{dP_0}
 =\prod_{a=1}^K(1+2\theta_a)^{N_{a1}}(1-2\theta_a)^{N_{a0}}.
\]
For \(\theta,\eta\in[-1/4,1/4]^K\), the Poisson probability generating function and independence over arms give
\[
 E_0[\Lambda_\theta\Lambda_\eta]
 =\prod_{a=1}^K
   \exp\!\left\{\frac\lambda2\bigl((1+2\theta_a)(1+2\eta_a)-1\bigr)
                   +\frac\lambda2\bigl((1-2\theta_a)(1-2\eta_a)-1\bigr)\right\}
 =e^{4\lambda\theta\cdot\eta}.
\]
Let \(\Delta=\nu_1-\nu_0\).  Normalization of the two priors gives \(\Delta([-1/4,1/4]^K)=0\).  By mixture linearity,
\[
 \frac{dP_{\nu_1}}{dP_0}-\frac{dP_{\nu_0}}{dP_0}
 =\int \Lambda_\theta\,d\Delta(\theta).
\]
The kernel \(e^{4\lambda\theta\cdot\eta}\) is bounded on the compact product cube.  Thus Fubini's theorem applies to the two finite signed measures, and
\[
 \left\|\frac{dP_{\nu_1}}{dP_0}-\frac{dP_{\nu_0}}{dP_0}\right\|_{L^2(P_0)}^2
 =\iint e^{4\lambda\theta\cdot\eta}\,d\Delta(\theta)d\Delta(\eta).
\]
The exponential series is absolutely and uniformly convergent on that product cube.  Its multi-index expansion therefore may be integrated term by term:
\[
 e^{4\lambda\theta\cdot\eta}
 =\sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^K}
   \frac{(4\lambda)^{|\alpha|}}{\alpha!}\theta^\alpha\eta^\alpha.
\]
Consequently the last double integral equals
\[
 \sum_{\alpha\in\mathbb N_0^K}
 \frac{(4\lambda)^{|\alpha|}}{\alpha!}
 \left\{\int\theta^\alpha\,d(\nu_1-\nu_0)(\theta)\right\}^2
 =\mathfrak D_{K,\lambda}(\nu_0,\nu_1).
\]
The term of degree zero is already zero by normalization.  If all mixed moments through total degree \(L\) agree, precisely the terms with \(1\leq|\alpha|\leq L\) vanish.  No condition has been imposed on moments of larger total degree, so their nonnegative weighted tail remains exactly as claimed.

statements.statement: For a patient group with local vector \(q=(q_{xa0},q_{xa1}:a\in[K])\), menu-scaled lower overlap implies \(F_K(q)=p_xm_x\). On the entire nonnegative orthant, \(F_K\) is degree-one homogeneous, satisfies \(0\le F_K(q)\le s(q)\), and is \((1+2K)\)-Lipschitz in \(\ell_1\). None of these conclusions uses an upper bound on \(e_{ax}\).
statements.justification: The extension is the full observational target seen by polynomial localization and proves that the upper logging cap is mathematically unnecessary.
statements.gap: Scalar factorial constructions do not address the conditional ratio at unknown patient-group and treatment masses; this lemma supplies the exact lower-overlap extension used by the joint certificate.
statements.consumer: The full-class estimator can localize on observed cell masses without estimating propensities or imposing an upper balance condition.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix a patient group \(x\), and put \(q_{ay}=q_{xay}\).  By the definitions of the observed cell probabilities,
\[
 s(q)=p_x,\quad s_a(q)=p_xe_{ax},\quad q_{a1}=p_xe_{ax}\mu_{ax}.
\]
If \(p_x=0\), then \(q=0\), and both \(F_K(q)\) and \(p_xm_x\) are zero.  If \(p_x>0\), \(\mathrm{ass{:}menu\text{-}scaled\text{-}overlap}\) gives \(s_a(q)\geq s(q)/(2K)\).  Hence the denominator in \(\mathrm{def{:}ratio\text{-}max\text{-}extension}\) is \(s_a(q)\), and
\[
 F_K(q)=\max_{a\in[K]}\frac{p_x\,p_xe_{ax}\mu_{ax}}{p_xe_{ax}}
       =p_x\max_{a\in[K]}\mu_{ax}=p_xm_x.
\]
Every division here is legitimate because \(p_xe_{ax}>0\).  This proves agreement with the identified contribution on every positive-mass cell.

For the extension properties, write
\[
 f_a(q)=\frac{s(q)q_{a1}}{\max\{s_a(q),s(q)/(2K)\}},
 \quad F_K(q)=\max_a f_a(q)
\]
for \(q\neq0\).  Positive homogeneity of numerator and denominator gives \(f_a(cq)=cf_a(q)\) for \(c\geq0\), including \(c=0\) by the declared convention.  Since \(q_{a1}\leq s_a(q)\leq\max\{s_a(q),s(q)/(2K)\}\),
\[
 0\leq f_a(q)\leq s(q),
\]
and the same bounds hold for their maximum.

It remains to prove the global Lipschitz statement.  On the half-space \(s_a(q)\leq s(q)/(2K)\), one has \(f_a(q)=2Kq_{a1}\), whose gradient has \(\ell_\infty\)-norm \(2K\).  On the other half-space, put \(z=q_{a1}\) and \(t=s_a(q)>0\).  Then \(f_a(q)=s(q)z/t\), with \(z/t\leq1\) and \(s(q)/t\leq2K\).  A coordinate outside arm \(a\) has derivative \(z/t\); the success coordinate has derivative
\[
 \frac zt+\frac{s(q)}t\left(1-\frac zt\right),
\]
and the failure coordinate has derivative
\[
 \frac zt-\frac{s(q)}t\frac zt.
\]
Each absolute derivative is at most \(1+2K\).  The two formulas for \(f_a\) agree on their common boundary.  A line segment in the nonnegative orthant crosses that linear boundary at most once unless it lies in it; integrating the directional derivative on the resulting subsegments gives
\[
 |f_a(q)-f_a(q')|\leq(1+2K)\|q-q'\|_1
\]
whenever neither endpoint is the origin.  If one endpoint is the origin, the same inequality follows from \(f_a(q)\leq s(q)=\|q\|_1\).  Finally,
\[
 |F_K(q)-F_K(q')|
 \leq\max_a|f_a(q)-f_a(q')|
 \leq(1+2K)\|q-q'\|_1.
\]
Only the lower-overlap inequality was used in the agreement step; all extension properties hold on the whole nonnegative orthant.  No upper bound on \(e_{ax}\) enters.

statements.statement: For independent \(N_j\sim\operatorname{Pois}(m q_j)\), \(E_q[G_h]=(q_j-z_j)^h\) and \[E_q[G_hG_t]=\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\{h,t\}}\binom h\ell\binom t\ell\ell!\,(q_j/m)^\ell(q_j-z_j)^{h+t-2\ell}.\] Consequently \(E_q[U_{Q_L}]=Q_L(q-z)\), and \(\operatorname{Var}_q(U_{Q_L})\) is the finite double sum over \(\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal A_{2K,L}\) obtained by multiplying the displayed coordinate second moments and subtracting \(Q_L(q-z)^2\).
statements.justification: This identity gives the complete finite covariance calculation for the actual unknown-mass, unknown-logging upper-bound coordinates.
statements.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015 supplies coordinatewise factorial lifts for additive functionals; the joint ratio maximum requires the full mixed double sum across \(2K\) coordinates.
statements.consumer: The certificate can audit the exact variance of every finite candidate table before using it in the full-class estimator.
statements.proof_tex:
For one coordinate \(j\), form the exponential generating function
\[
 \mathcal G_j(u):=\sum_{h\geq0}G_h(N_j;z_j,m)\frac{u^h}{h!}
 =e^{-z_ju}\left(1+\frac um\right)^{N_j}.
\]
The equality follows by multiplying the series for \(e^{-z_ju}\) and the falling-factorial expansion of \((1+u/m)^{N_j}\), and is coefficientwise the definition in \(\mathrm{def{:}observed\text{-}cell\text{-}factorial\text{-}lift}\).  Since \(N_j\sim\operatorname{Pois}(mq_j)\),
\[
 E_q[\mathcal G_j(u)]=e^{-z_ju}e^{q_ju}=e^{(q_j-z_j)u}.
\]
Thus \(E_q[G_h]=(q_j-z_j)^h\).  Likewise,
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_q[\mathcal G_j(u)\mathcal G_j(v)]
 &=e^{-z_j(u+v)}
   \exp\!\left(mq_j\left[\left(1+\frac um\right)
                                 \left(1+\frac vm\right)-1\right]\right)\\
 &=\exp\!\left((q_j-z_j)(u+v)+\frac{q_j}{m}uv\right).
 \end{aligned}
\]
Coefficient comparison gives exactly
\[
 E_q[G_hG_t]
 =\sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\{h,t\}}
   \binom h\ell\binom t\ell\ell!\,(q_j/m)^\ell
   (q_j-z_j)^{h+t-2\ell}.
\]
The required interchanges are finite coefficient calculations, and all Poisson factorial moments are finite.

For \(G_\alpha=\prod_{j=1}^{2K}G_{\alpha_j}(N_j;z_j,m)\), independence across the \(2K\) coordinates gives
\[
 E_q[G_\alpha]=(q-z)^\alpha
\]
and
\[
 E_q[G_\alpha G_\beta]
 =\prod_{j=1}^{2K}\left[
   \sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\{\alpha_j,\beta_j\}}
   \binom{\alpha_j}\ell\binom{\beta_j}\ell\ell!
   (q_j/m)^\ell(q_j-z_j)^{\alpha_j+\beta_j-2\ell}
 \right].
\]
Using the finite coefficient table in the definition therefore yields
\[
 E_q[U_{Q_L}]=\sum_\alpha\gamma_\alpha(q-z)^\alpha=Q_L(q-z),
\]
and the fully explicit finite variance
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \operatorname{Var}_q(U_{Q_L})
 =\sum_{\alpha,\beta\in\mathcal A_{2K,L}}\gamma_\alpha\gamma_\beta
 \Bigg\{&\prod_{j=1}^{2K}\left[
   \sum_{\ell=0}^{\min\{\alpha_j,\beta_j\}}
   \binom{\alpha_j}\ell\binom{\beta_j}\ell\ell!
   (q_j/m)^\ell(q_j-z_j)^{\alpha_j+\beta_j-2\ell}
 \right]\\
 &-(q-z)^{\alpha+\beta}\Bigg\}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This is the asserted finite double sum and includes every cross-monomial covariance.

statements.statement: On the Boolean restriction \(\theta_a\in\{-1/4,1/4\}\), an approximation to \(\max_{a\in[K]}\theta_a\) with uniform error at most \(1/56\) induces a \(1/14\)-approximation to signed \(\operatorname{OR}_K\); consequently its total degree is at least \(\sqrt K\).
statements.justification: This is the analytic early-kill test against a nominally dimension-free low-degree maximum certificate.
statements.gap: Spalek2008 proves the OR approximate-degree bound; the present reduction turns it into a non-representability constraint on the local statistical surrogate, while making no unsupported leap from degree to minimax risk.
statements.consumer: Every proposed certificate for the intermediate regime must either pay the square-root degree or exploit localization that avoids uniform Boolean approximation.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(p\) be a real polynomial on \(\mathbb R^K\) satisfying
\[
 \sup_{\theta\in\{-1/4,1/4\}^K}
 \left|p(\theta)-\max_{a\in[K]}\theta_a\right|\leq\frac1{56}.
\]
Use the signed Boolean convention in which the OR function is \(+1\) only at the all-\(+1\) input and is \(-1\) otherwise.  For \(x\in\{\pm1\}^K\), define the proof-intermediate polynomial
\[
 r(x)=-4p(-x/4).
\]
If every coordinate of \(x\) is \(+1\), then \(\max_a(-x_a/4)=-1/4\); otherwise at least one coordinate equals \(-1\), and that maximum is \(+1/4\).  Therefore
\[
 -4\max_a(-x_a/4)=\operatorname{OR}_K(x)
\]
under the stated signed convention, and hence
\[
 \sup_{x\in\{\pm1\}^K}|r(x)-\operatorname{OR}_K(x)|\leq4/56=1/14.
\]
Affine substitution and scalar multiplication do not increase total degree, so \(\deg r\leq\deg p\).  The cited lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}spalek\text{-}or\text{-}approximate\text{-}degree}\) says that such an approximant has degree at least \(\sqrt K\).  Thus \(\deg p\geq\sqrt K\), proving both conclusions.

statements.statement: There is an absolute constant \(C<\infty\) such that for every \(n,d,K\), \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,K}}E_{P^n}[(\widehat V_{\mathrm{ER}}-V^\star(P))^2]\le C\min\{1,u(d,K)/n\}\), uniformly over unknown \(p_x\), unknown \(e_{ax}\) satisfying only \(e_{ax}\ge1/(2K)\), null cells, exact ties, and boundary means.
statements.justification: This proves a full-class baseline with absolute constants, no oracle knowledge of masses or logging probabilities, and no upper balance restriction on logging.
statements.gap: NguyenBarrettJun2025HAVER conditions on externally supplied arm counts; the result here controls random causal cell occupancy and aggregation over arbitrary group masses.
statements.consumer: The estimator gives an immediately implementable attainable-value error guarantee for multi-arm causal forests and related treatment-targeting systems.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(P\in\mathcal M_{d,K}\).  For a group with \(N_x=k>0\), define
\[
 Z_x=\max_{a\in[K]}|\overline Y_{xa}-\mu_{ax}|.
\]
Conditional on \(N_x=k\), the arm count \(H=N_{xa}\) is \(\operatorname{Bin}(k,e_{ax})\).  The elementary exponential-moment calculation for this binomial variable gives
\[
 P(H<ke_{ax}/2\mid N_x=k)\leq e^{-ke_{ax}/8}.
\]
Indeed, Markov's inequality applied to \(e^{-(\log2)H}\), followed by \(1+u\leq e^u\), gives exponent
\(ke_{ax}\{(\log2)/2-1/2\}\leq-ke_{ax}/8\).

Given \(H=h>0\), the observed outcomes in that arm are independent Bernoulli variables of mean \(\mu_{ax}\).  For a Bernoulli variable \(W\) of mean \(\mu\), direct differentiation of
\(e^{-s\mu}(1-\mu+\mu e^s)\) gives
\(E[e^{s(W-\mu)}]\leq e^{s^2/8}\).  Markov's inequality, optimization over \(s\), and the same argument for \(-s\) therefore give
\[
 P(|\overline Y_{xa}-\mu_{ax}|>t\mid N_x=k,H=h)
 \leq2e^{-2ht^2}.
\]
For \(0<t\leq1\), splitting according to \(H<ke_{ax}/2\) yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 P(|\overline Y_{xa}-\mu_{ax}|>t\mid N_x=k)
 &\leq e^{-ke_{ax}/8}+2e^{-ke_{ax}t^2}\\
 &\leq3e^{-ke_{ax}t^2/8}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
This also covers the declared value at \(H=0\), because that event belongs to \(\{H<ke_{ax}/2\}\).  By the union bound and \(e_{ax}\geq1/(2K)\),
\[
 P(Z_x>t\mid N_x=k)
 \leq\min\left\{1,3K\exp\!\left(-\frac{kt^2}{16K}\right)\right\}.
\]
Since \(0\leq Z_x\leq1\), integration of this tail with \(s=t^2\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E[Z_x^2\mid N_x=k]
 &=\int_0^1P(Z_x>\sqrt s\mid N_x=k)\,ds\\
 &\leq C_0\min\left\{1,\frac{K\log(eK)}k\right\}
 \end{aligned}
\]
for an absolute \(C_0\).  To see the last inequality directly, split the integral at
\(16K\log(3K)/k\) when this number is below one; the remaining exponential integral is at most \(16K/k\).

By \(\mathrm{def{:}optimal\text{-}value}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}empirical\text{-}maximum}\), decompose
\[
 \widehat V_{\mathrm{ER}}-V^\star(P)=E_1+E_2,
\]
where
\[
 E_1=\sum_{x=1}^d\frac{N_x}{n}
 \left(\max_a\overline Y_{xa}-m_x\right),
 \quad
 E_2=\sum_{x=1}^d\left(\frac{N_x}{n}-p_x\right)m_x.
\]
The maximum map is one-Lipschitz in the sup norm, so the absolute value of the parenthesized term in \(E_1\) is at most \(Z_x\).  Since the nonnegative weights \(N_x/n\) sum to one, Jensen's inequality and the conditional bound above give
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_P[E_1^2]
 &\leq\sum_{x=1}^d E_P\left[\frac{N_x}{n}Z_x^2\right]\\
 &\leq\frac{C_0}{n}\sum_{x=1}^d K\log(eK)
 =\frac{C_0dK\log(eK)}n.
\end{aligned}
\]
The zero-count groups contribute zero, so no conditioning at \(k=0\) or division by zero occurs.  Under \(\mathrm{ass{:}iid\text{-}sampling}\),
\[
 E_2=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\{m_{X_i}-E_P[m_X]\}.
\]
Because \(0\leq m_X\leq1\), its variance is at most \(1/(4n)\).  Thus \((E_1+E_2)^2\leq2E_1^2+2E_2^2\) implies
\[
 E_{P^n}[(\widehat V_{\mathrm{ER}}-V^\star(P))^2]
 \leq C_1\frac{dK\log(eK)}n.
\]
Both the estimator and target lie in \([0,1]\), so their squared difference is also at most one.  Combining the two bounds, taking the supremum over \(P\), and recalling \(u(d,K)=dK\log(eK)\) proves the result with an absolute constant.  The proof used neither \(p_x>0\) for every group nor an upper bound, known value, or estimator of \(e_{ax}\); ties and boundary means were never excluded.

statements.statement: There is an absolute constant \(c>0\) such that for every \(n,d,K\), \(R(n,d,K)\ge c\min\{1,b(d,K)/n\}\); the lower experiment has \(p_x=1/d\), \(e_{ax}=1/K\), and centered random winners that preserve the arm-averaged conditional outcome mean in every patient group.
statements.justification: Centering removes the marginal outcome shift that weakens uncentered random-winner mixtures, and the uniform subexperiment remains legal under lower overlap alone.
statements.gap: CaiLow2011 and WuYang2016 give moment-mixture templates for other nonsmooth functionals; this exact winner-collision geometry is specific to grouped treatment maxima.
statements.consumer: The lower envelope rules out any analysis that obtains a falsely dimension-free or binary-like rate for expanding treatment menus.
statements.proof_tex:
It suffices by \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\text{-}risk}\) to construct a legal finite subexperiment.  Put \(p_x=1/d\) and \(e_{ax}=1/K\).  Under a proof-intermediate null law \(Q_0\), let every conditional outcome mean equal \(1/2\).  For each winner vector \(\mathbf j=(j_1,\ldots,j_d)\in[K]^d\) and \(0<\delta\leq1/4\), define an alternative law \(Q_{\mathbf j}\) by
\[
 \mu^{\mathbf j}_{ax}=\frac12+\eta_{\mathbf j,x,a},\quad
 \eta_{\mathbf j,x,a}=
 \begin{cases}
 \delta,&a=j_x,\\
 -\delta/(K-1),&a\neq j_x.
 \end{cases}
\]
These means belong to \([0,1]\), and their average over arms is exactly \(1/2\) in every group.  A full-data completion is obtained by drawing the potential outcomes conditionally on \(X=x\) as Bernoulli variables with these means, drawing \(A\) uniformly and independently of all potential outcomes conditional on \(X\), and setting \(Y=Y(A)\); give \(Q_0\) the same completion with all means equal to \(1/2\).  Every resulting law satisfies consistency, conditional exchangeability, and the overlap equality \(e_{ax}=1/K\geq1/(2K)\), so it belongs to \(\mathcal M_{d,K}\).  By \(\mathrm{def{:}optimal\text{-}value}\),
\[
 V^\star(Q_0)=\frac12,\quad V^\star(Q_{\mathbf j})=\frac12+\delta
\]
for every \(\mathbf j\).

For one observation, the likelihood ratio of \(Q_{\mathbf j}\) relative to \(Q_0\) at \((x,a,y)\) is
\[
 \Lambda_{\mathbf j}(x,a,y)=1+2(2y-1)\eta_{\mathbf j,x,a}.
\]
If \(h(\mathbf j,\mathbf l)=|\{x:j_x=l_x\}|\), direct summation over the \(2dK\) categories gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 E_{Q_0}[\Lambda_{\mathbf j}\Lambda_{\mathbf l}]
 &=1+\frac4{dK}\sum_{x=1}^d\sum_{a=1}^K
      \eta_{\mathbf j,x,a}\eta_{\mathbf l,x,a}\\
 &=1+\frac{4\delta^2\{K h(\mathbf j,\mathbf l)-d\}}
               {d(K-1)^2}.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Indeed, the inner product in a coincident-winner group is \(\delta^2K/(K-1)\), while in a different-winner group it is \(-\delta^2K/(K-1)^2\).  Let
\[
 Q_{\mathrm{mix}}=K^{-d}\sum_{\mathbf j\in[K]^d}Q_{\mathbf j}^{\,n}.
\]
For probability laws \(Q\ll P\), write
\(\chi^2(Q,P)=E_P[(dQ/dP-1)^2]\).
Independence of the observations and averaging two independent uniform winner vectors imply the exact identity
\[
 1+\chi^2(Q_{\mathrm{mix}},Q_0^n)
 =E\left[\left(1+\frac{4\delta^2(KH-d)}{d(K-1)^2}\right)^n\right],
 \quad H\sim\operatorname{Bin}(d,1/K).
\]
The base is positive because its minimum is \(1-4\delta^2/(K-1)^2>0\).  Define
\[
 u=\frac{4n\delta^2K}{d(K-1)^2}.
\]
Using \(1+z\leq e^z\), followed by the binomial moment generating function and \(\log(1+r)\leq r\), yields
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 \log\{1+\chi^2(Q_{\mathrm{mix}},Q_0^n)\}
 &\leq d\log\left[e^{-u/K}\left\{1+\frac{e^u-1}{K}\right\}\right]\\
 &\leq\frac dK(e^u-1-u).
 \end{aligned}
\]

Put \(w=K/d\), \(v=\log(1+\sqrt w)\), \(c_0=1/64\), and choose
\[
 \delta^2=c_0\min\left\{1,\frac{d(K-1)^2v}{nK}\right\}.
\]
Then \(\delta\leq1/8\) and, in both the saturated and unsaturated cases, \(0\leq u\leq4c_0v\).  For \(\psi(t)=e^t-1-t\), convexity and \(\psi(0)=0\) give \(\psi(4c_0v)\leq4c_0\psi(v)\).  Moreover,
\[
 \psi(v)=\sqrt w-\log(1+\sqrt w)
 =\int_0^{\sqrt w}\frac{t}{1+t}\,dt\leq\frac w2.
\]
It follows that
\[
 \log\{1+\chi^2(Q_{\mathrm{mix}},Q_0^n)\}\leq2c_0.
\]
Consequently, by Cauchy--Schwarz,
\[
 \operatorname{TV}(Q_{\mathrm{mix}},Q_0^n)
 \leq\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(Q_{\mathrm{mix}},Q_0^n)}
 \leq\frac12\sqrt{e^{2c_0}-1}=: \eta<\frac14.
\]
Here
\(\operatorname{TV}(Q,P)=\frac12\int|dQ-dP|\); the last strict inequality follows, for example, from
\(e^{1/32}\leq(1-1/32)^{-1}=32/31\).

For any estimator, threshold it at \(1/2+\delta/2\).  On a null testing error its squared estimation loss is at least \(\delta^2/4\), and the same is true on an alternative testing error.  The sum of the null error probability and the mixture-averaged alternative error probability is at least \(1-\eta\), by the defining variational inequality for total variation.  Hence the supremum risk over the constructed laws is at least
\[
 \frac{\delta^2}{8}(1-\eta).
\]
Finally,
\[
 \frac{(K-1)^2}{K^2}\geq\frac14,
 \quad
 \delta^2\geq\frac{c_0}{4}
 \min\left\{1,\frac{dK\log(1+\sqrt{K/d})}{n}\right\}.
\]
Taking the infimum over all estimators proves the asserted lower bound with an absolute constant.  The construction permits exact ties under the null and uses only a known-uniform subexperiment of the same full class.

statements.statement: For absolute constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), if \(K\ge d^2\) then \(c\min\{1,dK\log(eK)/n\}\le R(n,d,K)\le C\min\{1,dK\log(eK)/n\}\).
statements.justification: This is the first genuinely joint solved region and a non-negotiable splice for the full frontier.
statements.gap: No named published result gives minimax MSE for grouped causal optimal value in a jointly growing \(d,K\) region.
statements.consumer: Menu-expansion studies can read off the sample size required once the number of treatments dominates the square of patient-group count.
statements.proof_tex:
The upper inequality follows directly from \(\mathrm{lem{:}empirical\text{-}upper}\).  For the lower inequality, \(\mathrm{lem{:}centered\text{-}winner\text{-}lower}\) gives the scale
\[
 dK\log(1+\sqrt{K/d}).
\]
If \(K\geq d^2\), then \(d\leq\sqrt K\), so \(\sqrt{K/d}\geq K^{1/4}\) and
\[
 \log(1+\sqrt{K/d})\geq\frac14\log K.
\]
Since \(K\geq2\), one has \(1+\log K\leq(1+1/\log2)\log K<\frac52\log K\).  Therefore
\[
 \log(1+\sqrt{K/d})\geq\frac1{10}\log(eK).
\]
For \(0<\rho\leq1\), \(\min\{1,\rho z\}\geq\rho\min\{1,z\}\).  Applying this with \(\rho=1/10\) converts the centered-winner lower bound to the claimed lower rate.  Both constants remain absolute.

statements.statement: For absolute constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), \(c\min\{1,K\log(eK)/n\}\le R(n,1,K)\le C\min\{1,K\log(eK)/n\}\) for every \(n\ge1\) and \(K\ge2\); this adds the global bounded-Bernoulli all-estimator converse absent from the instance-dependent upper-bound theory of Nguyen, Barrett, and Jun, while leaving their easy-instance guarantees intact.
statements.justification: The passive one-group slice fixes the unavoidable \(\log K\) factor and prevents importing adaptive best-arm sample complexity.
statements.gap: NguyenBarrettJun2025HAVER proves sharp instance-dependent MSE upper bounds but no matching global minimax lower bound over bounded Bernoulli means.
statements.consumer: Maximum-mean estimation in Q-learning and Monte Carlo tree search gains a finite-sample worst-case benchmark for passive data.
statements.proof_tex:
Set \(d=1\) in \(\mathrm{lem{:}empirical\text{-}upper}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}centered\text{-}winner\text{-}lower}\).  The resulting upper scale is \(K\log(eK)\), while the lower scale is \(K\log(1+\sqrt K)\).  For \(K\geq2\),
\[
 \log(1+\sqrt K)\geq\frac12\log K
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \log(eK)=1+\log K<\frac52\log K.
\]
Thus \(\log(1+\sqrt K)\geq\frac15\log(eK)\).  The elementary relation \(\min\{1,\rho z\}\geq\rho\min\{1,z\}\) for \(0<\rho\leq1\) proves the two-sided benchmark with absolute constants.  The bibliographic scope assertion in the final clause is exactly the delivery distinction recorded in \(\mathrm{lem{:}haver\text{-}upper\text{-}bound\text{-}scope}\): that work provides estimator-specific MSE upper bounds, whereas the lower inequality just proved quantifies over all estimators on the bounded-Bernoulli class.  Its easy-instance upper guarantees are not altered by this converse.

statements.statement: For every \(K\ge2\), the channel \(\mathsf G_K\), together with its declared causal completion, maps each binary observed-data law with \(\pi_x\in[1/3,2/3]\) into \(\mathcal M_{d,K}\), preserves the unrestricted optimal value, and appends only a parameter-free within-block treatment label. Therefore there is an absolute constant \(c>0\) such that \(R(n,d,K)\ge c\min\{1,d/[n\log(ed)]\}\) for every \(n,d,K\).
statements.justification: The parameter-free arm splitting transfers the binary hardness uniformly to every treatment-menu size and is needed for the necessity of bounded patient-group complexity.
statements.gap: The accepted binary frontier stops at two treatments; this Blackwell reduction is a new many-arm transfer with constants independent of \(K\) and remains valid without an upper logging cap.
statements.consumer: The joint frontier must dominate the binary sparse-group boundary in every menu regime, ruling out formulas that lose the \(d/\log(ed)\) obstruction.
statements.proof_tex:
Start with a binary observed-data law, write \(p_x=P(X=x)\), \(\pi_x=P(B=1\mid X=x)\in[1/3,2/3]\), and let \(\mu_{bx}=E[Y\mid B=b,X=x]\).  Under \(\mathsf G_K\), an arm \(a\in G_b\) has propensity
\[
 e_{ax}=\frac{P(B=b\mid X=x)}{g_b}.
\]
Both binary block probabilities are at least \(1/3\), and \(g_b\leq\lceil K/2\rceil\).  For every \(K\geq2\),
\[
 3\lceil K/2\rceil\leq2K,
\]
where the odd case uses \(K\geq3\).  Hence \(e_{ax}\geq1/(2K)\) for every arm on every positive-mass group.  The declared completion in \(\mathrm{def{:}binary\text{-}grouping\text{-}channel}\) draws arm potential outcomes with mean \(\mu_{bx}\) for \(a\in G_b\), independently of \(A\) conditional on \(X\), and sets \(Y=Y(A)\).  It therefore satisfies conditional exchangeability and consistency, as well as the overlap condition, and belongs to \(\mathcal M_{d,K}\).

Every arm in \(G_b\) has conditional outcome mean \(\mu_{bx}\).  Thus \(\mathrm{def{:}optimal\text{-}value}\) gives
\[
 V^\star(\mathsf G_KP)
 =\sum_xp_x\max_{a\in[K]}\mu_{ax}
 =\sum_xp_x\max_{b\in\{0,1\}}\mu_{bx},
\]
which is the unrestricted binary optimal value.  Conditional on \((X,B,Y)\), the additional arm label is uniform on the fixed block \(G_B\); its law is parameter-free.

Write \(O_i^{(2)}=(X_i,B_i,Y_i)\) for the \(i\)-th binary observation.  Let \(T_K\) be any estimator in the many-arm experiment.  Projection onto \([0,1]\) cannot increase squared loss because the target is in \([0,1]\), so we may first clip \(T_K\) and thereby make it bounded.  Apply the channel independently to each binary observation and then Rao--Blackwellize over its auxiliary uniform labels:
\[
 T_2(O_1^{(2)},\ldots,O_n^{(2)})
 =E[T_K(\mathsf G_KO_1^{(2)},\ldots,\mathsf G_KO_n^{(2)})
       \mid O_1^{(2)},\ldots,O_n^{(2)}].
\]
Conditional Jensen's inequality and value preservation show that the risk of \(T_2\) at every binary law is no larger than the risk of \(T_K\) at its image law.  Taking the binary supremum and then the infimum over \(T_K\) shows that \(R(n,d,K)\) is at least the binary minimax risk.  The accepted result \texttt{stat\_discrete\_optimal\_value\_minimax\_matched/thm:matched-minimax-frontier} gives, for binary propensities in \([1/3,2/3]\), an absolute lower bound
\[
 c\min\left\{1,\frac{d}{n\log(ed)}\right\}.
\]
This proves the claimed transfer with a constant independent of \(K\).

statements.statement: For arbitrary sequences \((d_n,K_n)\) as \(n\to\infty\), \(R(n,d_n,K_n)=O(n^{-1})\) if and only if both \(d_n\) and \(K_n\) are bounded.
statements.justification: This gives a complete and dimension-uniform answer for when parametric MSE is possible even before the intermediate consistency frontier is closed.
statements.gap: LuedtkeVanderLaan2016 studies fixed-complexity regularity. The static theorem in WhitehouseAusternSyrgkanis2025 assumes a \(\delta\)-polynomial density for each suboptimality gap, \(\beta_n=\omega(n^{1/[2(1+\delta)]})\), specified \(L^2\) nuisance rates, uniform boundedness, and positive limiting variance; neither paper gives the necessary-and-sufficient unrestricted \((d_n,K_n)\) minimax criterion.
statements.consumer: Practitioners can distinguish benign fixed-menu asymptotics from regimes where expanding personalization complexity necessarily destroys parametric accuracy.
statements.proof_tex:
Suppose first that \(d_n\leq D\) and \(K_n\leq K_0\) for all sufficiently large \(n\), where \(D\) and \(K_0\) are finite.  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}empirical\text{-}upper}\),
\[
 R(n,d_n,K_n)
 \leq C\frac{d_nK_n\log(eK_n)}n
 \leq\frac{CDK_0\log(eK_0)}n.
\]
Thus the risk is \(O(n^{-1})\).

For the converse, first note directly from \(\mathrm{def{:}law\text{-}class}\) and \(\mathrm{def{:}minimax\text{-}risk}\) that
\[
 R(n,d,K)\geq R(n,1,K).
\]
Indeed, embed any one-group law by assigning mass one to group \(1\) and mass zero to all other groups; the resulting data experiment is isomorphic to the one-group experiment, and all added cells are null.  If \((K_n)\) is unbounded, choose a subsequence along which \(K_n\to\infty\).  The preceding embedding and \(\mathrm{thm{:}one\text{-}group\text{-}benchmark}\) give along that subsequence
\[
 nR(n,d_n,K_n)\geq c\min\{n,K_n\log(eK_n)\}\longrightarrow\infty.
\]
Hence \(R(n,d_n,K_n)\) cannot be \(O(n^{-1})\).

If \((d_n)\) is unbounded, choose a subsequence along which \(d_n\to\infty\).  By \(\mathrm{lem{:}binary\text{-}grouping\text{-}transfer}\),
\[
 nR(n,d_n,K_n)
 \geq c\min\left\{n,\frac{d_n}{\log(ed_n)}\right\}
 \longrightarrow\infty,
\]
because both entries of the minimum diverge on that subsequence.  Thus parametric MSE also fails whenever \((d_n)\) is unbounded.  An integer sequence is bounded exactly when it has no subsequence tending to infinity, so the two arguments establish necessity without any monotonicity assumption.

statements.statement: The constructed law \(P_{\mathrm{wit}}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_{2,3}\), has unequal propensities, has maximizing arm \(a=1\) at \(x=1\) and maximizing arm \(a=3\) at \(x=2\), and satisfies \(V^\star(P_{\mathrm{wit}})=43/50\).
statements.justification: The explicit law catches accidental assumptions of uniform logging or a common maximizing treatment across groups.
statements.gap: This is an internal specification witness rather than a novelty claim; it tests the exact scope omitted by one-group and fixed-policy analyses.
statements.consumer: Formalization and estimator definitions receive a concrete regression test with switching winners and legal unequal treatment probabilities.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{def{:}unequal\text{-}logging\text{-}witness}\), \(d=2\), \(K=3\), and \(p_1=p_2=1/2\).  Thus both groups have positive mass and the displayed conditional treatment probabilities are
\[
(e_{11},e_{21},e_{31})=(1/2,1/3,1/6),
\qquad
(e_{12},e_{22},e_{32})=(1/6,1/3,1/2).
\]
Each vector has sum
\[
\frac12+\frac13+\frac16=1,
\]
so each is a probability vector.  Moreover, every displayed entry is at least
\[
\frac16=\frac{1}{2K}.
\]
Consequently the menu-scaled overlap condition in \(\mathrm{def{:}law\text{-}class}\) holds on every positive-mass group.  (In fact every entry is also at most \(1/2<2/3=2/K\).)  The two propensity vectors are unequal within each group, and they also differ across the two groups; hence the logging propensities are unequal.

The same construction draws \(A\), conditionally on \(X\), independently of the entire vector \((Y(1),Y(2),Y(3))\).  Therefore
\[
(Y(1),Y(2),Y(3))\mathrel{\perp}A\mid X,
\]
which is the conditional-exchangeability condition appearing in \(\mathrm{def{:}law\text{-}class}\).  It then sets \(Y=Y(A)\), so the consistency condition in that definition holds almost surely.  Together with the verified overlap condition, these facts give
\[
P_{\mathrm{wit}}\in\mathcal M_{2,3}.
\]

For the first group, the conditional means specified by the construction obey
\[
\mu_{11}=\frac9{10}>\mu_{21}=\frac12>\mu_{31}=\frac15.
\]
Thus the unique maximizing arm at \(x=1\) is \(a=1\), and \(m_1=9/10\) by the definition of \(m_x\).  For the second group,
\[
\mu_{32}=\frac{41}{50}>\mu_{22}=\frac35>\mu_{12}=\frac14.
\]
Thus the unique maximizing arm at \(x=2\) is \(a=3\), and \(m_2=41/50\).  Finally, the identifying formula in \(\mathrm{def{:}optimal\text{-}value}\) yields
\[
\begin{aligned}
V^\star(P_{\mathrm{wit}})
  &=\sum_{x=1}^{2}p_xm_x \\
  &=\frac12\left(\frac9{10}\right)
    +\frac12\left(\frac{41}{50}\right) \\
  &=\frac{45}{100}+\frac{41}{100}
   =\frac{86}{100}
   =\frac{43}{50}.
\end{aligned}
\]
This proves every asserted property.

statements.statement: Can one construct and evaluate \(\mathfrak J(d,K,\lambda,L)\) with absolute constants so that the full observed-cell polynomial \(Q_L\) approximates \(F_K(q)\) with controlled exact factorial covariance, while its balanced-slice reduction matches normalized dual-prior separation and weighted mixture distance uniformly in \(K\), respects the \(\sqrt K\) Boolean obstruction, and remains stable after localization over arbitrary patient-group masses and propensities satisfying only \(e_{ax}\ge1/(2K)\)? The construction must output finite coefficient tables and a terminating exact certificate routine.
statements.justification: This is the genuinely open mathematical content: uniform approximation error alone is insufficient unless the same object controls estimator variance and lower-mixture distinguishability.
statements.gap: JiaoVenkatHanWeissman2015, WuYang2016, and CaiLow2011 provide scalar templates, while Spalek2008 supplies only the Boolean degree obstruction; none closes their multivariate statistical combination.
statements.consumer: A solution closes the presently unmatched region \(2<K<d^2\) and supplies an auditable finite statistic for other sparse maxima over growing coordinate sets.

obligation.what_is_open: A dimension-uniform construction of the finite polynomial tables and normalized dual priors with matching approximation, exact factorial-covariance, target-separation, and weighted mixed-moment bounds throughout \(2<K<d^2\), stable under localization for arbitrary patient-group masses and every propensity vector satisfying only the stated lower overlap.
obligation.obstruction: The proved identities expose but do not control the weighted derivative and moment tails. Uniform approximation alone is insufficient, and the cited OR theorem rules out any fixed-relative-error full-Boolean-cube certificate of degree below \(\sqrt K\). No frozen assumption or established node supplies coefficient envelopes, matching legal priors, product-mixture closeness, or mass-localization control with constants independent of \(K\).
obligation.attempted: The balanced Poisson generating functions were expanded exactly on both primal and dual sides; the full observed-cell falling-factorial covariance was evaluated; the ratio-max extension was checked on the whole orthant; and the Boolean reduction was wired to the sharp published approximate-degree obstruction. These steps leave the simultaneous coefficient/variance and normalized-prior tail construction unresolved.
obligation.partial_result: The exact primal identities are now proved: the balanced lift has bias \(\mathcal E_K(P_L)\) and derivative-weighted variance \(\mathcal W_{K,\lambda}(P_L)\), while the observed-cell lift has the displayed finite covariance matrix for arbitrary local masses and logging.  The exact dual kernel is \(\mathfrak D_{K,\lambda}\), and uniform error below \(1/56\) on the Boolean slice forces degree at least \(\sqrt K\).  What remains unproved is an explicit family of finite coefficient tables and normalized priors whose approximation error, exact factorial covariance, target separation, and weighted moment tail have matching absolute-constant orders uniformly in \(K\), followed by localization over arbitrary \(p_x\) and legal \(e_{ax}\).

statements.statement: Derive an explicit closed-form \(r_\star(n,d,K)\), including every logarithmic, transition, and saturation branch, construct the total statistically computable estimator \(\widehat V_\star\) with the finite representation and evaluation bound in \(\mathrm{def{:}frontier\text{-}estimator\text{-}handle}\), and prove with absolute constants \(0<c<C<\infty\) that \(c r_\star(n,d,K)\le R(n,d,K)\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_{d,K}}E_{P^n}[(\widehat V_\star-V^\star(P))^2]\le C r_\star(n,d,K)\) for every \(n,d,K\); use the evaluated rate to characterize exactly when \(R(n,d_n,K_n)\to0\) for arbitrary dimension sequences.
statements.justification: The evaluated joint frontier, together with an auditable finite estimator rather than an unevaluated optimization, is the theorem-level kernel promised by the topic.
statements.gap: No published comparator supplies both sides of this full-class jointly growing \(d,K\) risk. The accepted \(K=2\) result is only a cited boundary condition; the new work begins with the many-arm grouping transfer and the \(K\)-uniform certificate.
statements.consumer: The result becomes the unrestricted attainable-value benchmark against which multi-arm causal forests and observational treatment-targeting methods can report the statistical price of expanding menus.

obligation.what_is_open: The explicit sharp risk scale and total attaining estimator in the intermediate region \(2<K<d^2\), together with the necessary-and-sufficient consistency boundary for arbitrary \(d_n,K_n\).
obligation.obstruction: The fixed-sample winner lower bound and empirical upper bound have different orders in part of the intermediate region. Closing that gap requires the unresolved dimension-uniform certificate, followed by absolute-constant localization and fixed-sample aggregation. The current core contains no result that turns the exact local identities into a sharper full-class estimator or a matching same-class converse.
obligation.attempted: The empirical estimator was optimized without unknown nuisance inputs, the centered-winner mixture was evaluated exactly including saturation, the one-group and large-menu regions were matched, and the binary experiment was transferred by a parameter-free channel. These produce an explicit honest bracket but not equality of its two scales in the central region.
obligation.partial_result:
The proved fixed-sample bracket is
\[
 c\min\!\left\{1,\frac{\max\{d/\log(ed),\ dK\log(1+\sqrt{K/d})\}}{n}\right\}
 \leq R(n,d,K)
 \leq C\min\!\left\{1,\frac{dK\log(eK)}n\right\}.
\]
It is sharp for \(K\geq d^2\), is sharp for \(d=1\), and combines with the accepted binary frontier on \(K=2\).  The total empirical estimator attains the displayed upper bound, and the parametric-MSE condition is exactly bounded \((d_n)\) and bounded \((K_n)\).  The explicit intermediate-region rate, an attaining estimator at that sharper rate, and the necessary-and-sufficient general consistency condition remain unresolved because the dimension-uniform certificate has not been constructed.

statements.statement: For every integer \(K\geq2\), every real polynomial that uniformly approximates the signed Boolean OR function on \(\{\pm1\}^K\) with error at most \(1/14\) has total degree at least \(\sqrt K\).
